p11 supports the principle that sufficient cause under s.5 must cover the whole period, which a9 applies analogously to the proviso of s.15(2).
p11 establishes that under s.5 Limitation Act sufficient cause must cover the whole period of delay, supporting h1's holding that the second proviso to s.15(2) Payment of Wages Act requires the same.
Holding h3 explicitly references the Ruby Mills (p2) decision dated May 2, 1952, as the point after which appellants failed to show sufficient cause for delay, using it to ground the factual finding.

p6 holds that once reasonable cause is shown for failure within 6 months there is no further limitation, supporting a8's argument that showing sufficient cause removes the bar with no need to explain subsequent delay.
